purpose: Prevent one-set/one-unit assumptions and prevent silhouette claims from being made before the physical role and attachment of each identity-bearing assembly is understood.
requiredAnalysisOrder: Audit the complete set inventory and every separately built model before assigning the set to an RTS asset.
Map detachable subassemblies, repeated modules, minifigures, equipment, resources and opposing-faction builds separately.
Name the physical role, parent connection and contact behavior of every identity-bearing assembly before describing silhouette or locomotion.
Cross-check the construction sequence against the completed model and at least one final/product view before making a topology or appendage-count claim.
Record source fact, canon-derived adaptation, game-derived proposal and unresolved interpretation as different states.
Compare all plausible construction methods and disclose the exact source components before asking the game director to approve a composed design.

candidateConstructionMethods.description: Preserve one official model's dominant masses and mechanisms while adapting only what canon or RTS readability requires.
Promote one detachable or independently built module from a larger official model into the basis of a different roster asset.
Combine clearly named modules from multiple approved official sources while preserving their connection logic and faction grammar.
Use an official game's recombination of recognizable source modules as an ideation pattern, then propose an original project-specific arrangement rather than copying it.
Design a new asset from recurring official connection, support, tool, cockpit, tube or production-exit grammar when no direct model exists.
Start from the canonical gameplay footprint and required readable mechanism, then justify every visible mass with approved source modules or faction construction grammar.

gameReferencePool.allowedUse: Official-game unit/building composition and motion ideation; no direct copying.

gameReferencePool.title: LEGO Battles (Nintendo DS)
gameReferencePool.allowedUse: LEGO-scale RTS readability, modular building and unit-combination ideation; not source canon.

caseStudies.finding: The complete source is a low open hovercraft with two forward ice saws, two raised round side hover/engine pods, a central hazard panel and an exposed Sparks operator; it is not a wheeled single-drill vehicle.
caseStudies.productionConsequence: The canonical Drill Craft may retain its single oversized mining drill only as a labeled adaptation of the source tool package. The flat hover sled, paired side lift masses and open operator relationship are the source-grounded chassis language.

caseStudies.finding: The source is the five named crew minifigures plus a very small equipment/control stand, loose tools including a handheld saw assembly, and a crystal boulder; it contains no major vehicle.
caseStudies.productionConsequence: Treat Rock Raider Crew as a shared worker class with visible character/equipment variants. Do not invent a 4930-derived vehicle or promote the small stand into the crew's body.

caseStudies.finding: The Worker Robot source has one shallow central operator wedge and two mirrored articulated legs ending in broad feet. The completed model and cover show a bipedal walker; there are not four radial outriggers.
caseStudies.productionConsequence: Preserve the tiny open biped and add any canonical worker manipulator as a clearly subordinate adaptation. Never infer appendage count from a top-like silhouette without following the build connections.

caseStudies.finding: The Mothership instructions build and dock several independently readable modules: the main circular carrier, a long front/central lime-conduit craft, two small seated weapon craft and two disc-like alien jetpack modules.
caseStudies.productionConsequence: One large set may supply multiple roster assets or building modules. Record each detachable assembly and its candidate use instead of treating the boxed set as one indivisible unit.

caseStudies.finding: The CrystAlien Conflict Training Camp uses a 2-by-2 repetition of low white-orange nose/cockpit modules that visibly echo the Recon Dropship family.
caseStudies.productionConsequence: This is the approved kind of ideation precedent when no set is a direct building match: identify the donor module, explain the repetition and function, propose alternatives, and obtain director approval before production. It is a method reference, not a design to copy.

knownAuditCorrection.incorrectClaim: The source was described as a four-spoke platform with four end pads and the bipedal reading was rejected.
knownAuditCorrection.rootCause: The audit counted visible appendage-like masses from a final angle without tracing the two mirrored leg assemblies through the construction sequence or assigning their physical parent and ground-contact role.
knownAuditCorrection.preventiveGuard: Any topology, locomotion or negative physical claim must cite both a construction-sequence connection and a completed-model view; the semantic part map must name each appendage's parent and contact function first.

packetNotice: A source set is a container of models, figures, equipment and detachable modules, not an automatic one-to-one unit mapping. Any composed design must disclose its exact donor components, adaptation and rejected alternatives before director approval.
